title: Quantization profile gating: baseline selection (per model family/GPU SKU) + compatibility checks + required eval suites
creator: Noah Patel
description:
Context
Optimize can recommend switching quantization profiles (ex: fp16 -> int8, int8 -> fp8, per-layer mixed precision) to reduce $/token. These changes can introduce correctness/quality regressions that don’t show up as simple latency/cost deltas. For quality gating to be meaningful, we need:
1) a deterministic baseline selection strategy (what do we compare against?) that respects model family + GPU SKU, and
2) hard compatibility checks before we even run expensive evals (prevent “passes eval but crashes/changes semantics under load”).

This ticket covers quantization-specific behavior only. Batching/cache gates are handled elsewhere.

Links
- System design: confluence://product-docs/design-specs/optimize-quality-gates-system-design
- Gate metrics/thresholds: confluence://applied-ml-and-evals/quality-guardrails/quality-gate-metrics-and-thresholds-v1
- Eval-harness contract: confluence://applied-ml-and-evals/eval-harness/gating-integration-contracts
- Runtime config diff safety notes: drive://engineering/serving-runtime/config-diff-safety-notes

Problem statement
Quantization “baseline” is not universal:
- Quality deltas differ by model family (Llama vs Mixtral vs Qwen, etc.) and by GPU SKU (H100 fp8 path vs A100 int8 path, etc.).
- Some routes currently run a non-default profile (hotfixed for stability). Comparing against a global default would show a false “improvement/regression”.
- If a recommended profile is incompatible with the model’s serving topology (TP/PP), KV-cache dtype, or kernel availability on the target SKU, the eval run is wasted and/or misleading.

Scope / deliverables
A) Baseline selection logic for quantization gate runs
Define baseline selection for a proposed quant profile change on a specific (route, model, hardware sku) target.

Baseline resolution order (v1):
1. Route-pinned baseline: if route has an explicit currently-effective quant_profile_id for the target model version + target sku, use that.
2. Account-tier default baseline: if no route pin exists, use default quant profile for (model family, sku, tier) from runtime registry.
3. Model family default baseline: if tier-specific is missing, use (model family, sku) default.
4. Fallback: block with a clear error and require manual baseline pinning (no silent fallback across SKUs).

Notes:
- Baseline is selected per GPU SKU. We do NOT compare H100(fp8) candidate vs A100(int8) baseline even if same model version.
- Baseline selection is done at gate-run creation time and stored on the gate_run record for auditability.
- If the “current effective” profile changes during the gate run (concurrent config updates), gate run completes but cannot be applied; Optimize must re-run with a fresh baseline.

B) Required eval suites for quant profile changes
Quantization changes must run the “full” gate tier by default (smoke is insufficient); exception only for internal/dev routes.

Required suites (initial list; exact prompt-set IDs live in eval-harness registry):
- General instruction-following + refusal policy suite (rubric-scored)
- Structured output / JSON validity suite (strict parser + schema checks)
- Tool/function calling formatting suite (strict)
- Long-context stability suite (sensitive to fp8/int8 + KV behavior; includes 8k/16k contexts)
- Math/logic suite (variance tracked; use paired prompts)
- Multilingual sanity suite (short)

Acceptance requirement: gate run must report per-suite deltas + aggregate decision, and include “sensitivity flags” for suites known to be quantization-sensitive (long-context, structured output).

C) Compatibility checks (pre-gate static validation)
Before calling eval-harness, validate candidate profile compatibility. Fail fast with a user-facing reason and a machine-readable reason_code.

Checks (v1):
- Model family compatibility: profile must list supported model families/architectures.
- GPU SKU compatibility: profile must list supported SKUs; no implicit “close enough” mapping.
- Kernel availability: required kernel set (ex: fp8 GEMM kernels) available in target region/image release; otherwise block.
- Serving topology constraints: profile must support current TP/PP and max batch scheduling mode (continuous batching).
- KV-cache dtype constraint: prevent combos known to corrupt outputs (ex: fp8 weights + unsupported kv-cache quant mode).
- Known-bad combos catalog: block profiles flagged as “unsafe_for_prod” or “experimental_only”.

Implementation details
- Add QuantBaselineResolver in Optimize service (or shared gating lib) with deterministic resolution + audit fields:
  - baseline_quant_profile_id
  - baseline_source (route_pin | tier_default | family_default)
  - baseline_model_family
  - baseline_gpu_sku
- Extend gating payload sent to eval-harness to include explicit baseline_profile_id and candidate_profile_id (no implicit defaults inside harness).
- Add quant profile registry lookup from runtime config registry (existing service) and cache with short TTL.
- Add reason codes for compatibility failures, eg:
  - QUANT_PROFILE_UNSUPPORTED_MODEL_FAMILY
  - QUANT_PROFILE_UNSUPPORTED_GPU_SKU
  - QUANT_PROFILE_KERNELS_UNAVAILABLE
  - QUANT_PROFILE_UNSUPPORTED_TOPOLOGY
  - QUANT_PROFILE_UNSAFE_FLAG
  - BASELINE_NOT_FOUND_BLOCKED

Acceptance criteria
- For any quantization profile config diff, Optimize creates a gate run with baseline_profile_id and baseline_source set.
- Gate creation blocks if baseline cannot be resolved (no cross-SKU fallback).
- Gate creation blocks if compatibility validation fails, returning a stable reason_code and a user-readable message surfaced in Console.
- Quantization profile changes default to “full gates required” policy (unless route policy explicitly opts into smoke via internal-only flag).
- Gate results include per-suite deltas for the required quant suites and aggregate pass/fail.
- Audit: baseline resolution and compatibility decision are persisted and visible via gate run API.

Rollout / risk notes
- Risk: false blocks for routes using legacy profile IDs not present in the registry.
  - Mitigation: add migration mapping for legacy IDs and a one-time backfill for top enterprise routes.
- Risk: gate runtime increases (full suites) and could slow Optimize.
  - Mitigation: enforce suite-level timeouts; allow manual override pathway (handled in override policy ticket) with explicit “quant gate bypass” reason.

Testing plan
- Unit tests for baseline resolver (matrix of route pins, tier defaults, missing defaults, sku mismatch).
- Unit tests for compatibility validator reason codes.
- Integration test: create gate run for H100 + Llama3 with candidate fp8 profile; verify baseline picked from route pin; verify payload includes both profile IDs.
- Negative integration test: H100-only profile recommended for A100 route -> blocked with QUANT_PROFILE_UNSUPPORTED_GPU_SKU.

Follow-ups (not blocking Done)
- Add region-awareness to kernel availability check (currently uses serving image release only; region-specific drift can still happen).
- Consider adding “paired evaluation” mode for quant changes (same random seeds / determinism knobs) to reduce variance in pass/fail.
